correctness.rationale: The bipartite adjacency follower block has exact singular-value trace formula (1). Exhaustive three-vertex orbit classification gives exactly A, M, U. Class A has Gram spectrum 1 repeated n−4 and n²−5n+7; M has spectrum 1 repeated n−3 and the same collective eigenvalue; U has spectrum 1 repeated n−4 plus a two-dimensional block with trace n²−5n+9 and determinant 2. Substitution into the trace formula gives the three stated rational costs; symbolic cancellation verifies both strict gaps 2/[n(n−2)(n−1)] and 2(n−1)(2n²−9)/[3n(n−2)(3n²−8n+3)], positive for every integer n≥4. Replayed verification program independently computes 1340 exact grounded-Laplacian inverses for n=3..8. Finite checks do not substitute for the all-n proof.

originality.rationale: The full inspected Fitch–Leonard arXiv:1407.1569 develops general joint centrality and proves explicit optimal m-leader spacing on cycles; that implies the n=3 six-cycle case, explicitly excluded, but does not imply the three symmetry-class inverse-trace ordering of crown graphs n≥4. Inspected Patterson–McGlohon–Dyagilev arXiv:1412.6595 treats paths and rings via one-dimensional decomposition, not the n≥4 crown. Direct matching object-and-invariant published-record searches surfaced only other crown graph invariants and unrelated finite-crown posets. General formulae alone require new graph-specific spectral calculation, strict inequalities and exhaustive orbit comparison. No stronger covering theorem was identified in accessible checks, with residual unindexed-literature uncertainty.

value.rationale: A crown graph models two fully cross-connected communities except one systematically missing pair per vertex. Three leaders generate not just one mixed versus unmixed distinction but three symmetry types, and the missing matching induces a strict and non-obvious secondary mixed-class ranking. The result supplies exact costs, complete optimizers and 2*C(n,3) counts for all n≥4. The distinct cost gaps quantify sensitivity to paired versus unpaired mixed placements, a concrete robust-sensor/leader design choice; this is not an arbitrary finite enumeration or a relabelled complete bipartite result.
